NEWS FROM THE BOARD February 2025 NEWS FROM THE BOARD A monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners Welcome to the monthly newsletter from the Ada County Board of Commissioners. We are happy to share information on significant news and events in Ada County. Ryan Davidson - Commissioner Rod Beck - Chairman Tom Dayley - Commissioner Professional soccer is coming to Idaho and fans throughout the northwest are ready for it! Ada County is partnering with Boise Pro Soccer to create a world-class soccer facility on the Expo Idaho Property. Soon, a future Lionel Messi or Abby Wambach will kick goals just a ten-minute drive from downtown Boise. A 30-year lease and development agreement signed by the Ada County Commissioners on February 21, 2025, uses zero tax dollars to create this first-of-its-kind facility in Idaho. Boise Pro Soccer will upgrade and remodel Ada County’s Turf Club and Grandstands at Expo Idaho and build professional soccer fields in an area where horses used to race ten years ago. What’s even better is that part of the revenue generated from the new facility will cover the maintenance and upkeep of The Park at Expo Idaho. That 50-acre project is being built along the Boise River Greenbelt and will be completed in 2026. The two areas, adjacent to one another, create an oasis of outdoor spaces and sports facilities that will attract visitors from around the northwest. We hope you’ll continue following along with the progress on both projects! adacounty.id.gov Learn more about Boise Pro Soccer: www.boiseprosoccer.com

ADA COUNTY LANDFILL PRESENTATION The audience at the February 13, 2025 Downtown Rotary Club was keenly interested in Ada County Landfill Director Herb Cantu’s presentation about the operations at this state of the art facility. Prior to the presentation Herb gave the group a reading assignment about the troubled Chiquita Canyon Landfill in California, which underscores the importance of effective and responsible management of landfills. Herb loves talking trash and the attendees asked excellent questions about landfill operations, the landfill’s history and location, and how Ada County is expanding its lifespan. Learn more about the Ada County Landfill: adacounty.id.gov/landfill/ Learn More about Career Opportunities and Ada County’s Benefits Package https://adacounty.id.gov/human-resources/ 3

PUBLIC INFORMATION OFFICER (PIO) TRAINING Getting the Right Information to the Right People at the Right Time When there is an emergency in your community what are your trusted sources for reliable and useful information? If, for instance, there was a need to evacuate or to prepare for a disaster, what sources consistently provide the most accurate information? Public Information Officers (PIOs) who work for state, county, city and tribal governments in Idaho work each day to make sure you have the right information at the right time. This does not just apply to emergencies. PIOs are the source for information on new programs, laws, and initiatives originating from government agencies that affect all our lives. Ada County Emergency Management and Community Resilience (ACEM) was proud to host a three-day Public Information Officer training in Boise in February. PIOs from around Idaho and Washington attended. The group included state agencies like the Tax Commission, Department of Environmental Quality (DEQ), the Idaho Office of Emergency Management (IOEM), Boise Fire, Cal Fire, the Boise Airport and several health districts. The PIO Basic Course provides essential skills in public information management, media relations, and effective messaging during incidents. Participants learn the fundamentals of gathering, verifying, and disseminating critical information to the public, ensuring transparency and trust during emergencies. At the heart of these classes is a focus on making sure information is easy to understand and easily accessible so people can make decisions based on facts for themselves and their families. Thank you to the Idaho Office of Emergency Management for making these and other important classes and training opportunities available. Thank you to our instructors - Ada County Communications Manager Elizabeth Duncan and Former Idaho Falls Fire Chief Dave Hanneman for sharing their real-world experience and making this hands-on training practical and meaningful. This course is funded through the State Homeland Security Grant Program (SHSGP) “By investing in this progressive training model, we can ensure that our community remains prepared, informed, and capable of handling evolving challenges in emergency management.” Agencies in attendance included: Ada County Ada County Highway District American Red Cross Boise Airport Boise Fire Dept. Butte County Cal Fire Caldwell Fire Department City of Pullman, WA Department of Environmental Quality Idaho Division of Occupational and Professional Licenses Idaho State Tax Commission Idaho State University Idaho Transportation Department IOEM Meridian Police Department Molalla Fire District Shoshone-Bannock Tribes South Central Public Health 4

The Ada County Recorder’s Office will be temporarily closed to the public on Friday, April 4, 2025, as a new recording software is being implemented. The new recording system will launch on Monday April 7, 2025, and operations will resume as normal. Due to the required closure, all functions of the Recorder’s Office will not be accessible to the public on Friday April 4, 2025 until Monday, April 7, 2025. Services such as obtaining marriage licenses, passports and passport photos, catering permits, alcohol beverage license renewals, copies, any research and property record recordings will be unavailable during this period. We apologize for any inconvenience this may cause and appreciate your understanding. During this time, we encourage you to schedule appointments early or explore our online resources and services, which may offer alternatives or allow you to prepare in advance for when the office reopens on April 7, 2025. If you have urgent matters or require assistance, please do not hesitate to contact us at (208)-287-6840 or visit our website adacounty.id.gov/clerk/license-permits/. IMPORTANT INFORMATION ABOUT ADA COUNTY ALCOHOL BEVERAGE LICENSES The Ada County Recorder’s Office will be launching the new recording system on April 7, 2025. Any alcohol beverage license renewals that are not submitted by March 28, 2025, will need to wait until after April 7, 2025, to be submitted. Our office must clear the current recording system prior to launching the new system. To avoid any delays, please submit your alcohol beverage li- cense renewal early. To renew your alcohol license, please have a pdf copy of your 2026 State of Idaho Al- cohol Beverage License available to be uploaded. If you have any ques- tions, please contact our staff at alcohol.licensing@adacounty.id.gov or (208) 287-6840. ADA COUNTY GOVERNMENT In addition to elected offices, Ada County government includes thirteen individual departments. Each department provides important services to our residents in Star, Eagle, Meridian, Boise, Garden City, Kuna, and Unincorporated Ada County. These services include law enforcement protection, emergency preparedness, election services, parks & waterways, indigent services, juvenile services, solid waste management, the Western Idaho Fair, Weed, Pest & Mosquito Abatement and more.
